headline: United's capacity response to fuel prices cannot be told apart from zero: 4 quarters after a 10% rise in jet fuel, United's capacity growth differs by +0.12 points (90% range -0.11 to +0.35) over 24 quarters (2014Q1 to 2019Q4), and the second specification gives +0.43 points (90% range +0.19 to +0.66); the two do not agree, so no response is established.
plain_summary: United's capacity response to fuel prices cannot be told apart from zero: 4 quarters after a 10% rise in jet fuel, United's capacity growth differs by +0.12 points (90% range -0.11 to +0.35) over 24 quarters (2014Q1 to 2019Q4), and the second specification gives +0.43 points (90% range +0.19 to +0.66); the two do not agree, so no response is established. By quarter after a 10% fuel rise (P10, P50, P90, points of capacity growth): quarter 0: -0.31, -0.08, +0.17; quarter 1: -0.13, +0.10, +0.33; quarter 2: -0.13, +0.09, +0.30; quarter 3: +0.03, +0.26, +0.48; quarter 4: -0.05, +0.13, +0.31. The other specification (no other regressor) gives +0.43 points (90% range +0.19 to +0.66) after 4 quarters. Of the 4 variants estimated without test-year quarters, 0 show capacity lower a year after fuel rises and 2 show it higher. In 2024Q1 to 2026Q2 (10 quarters) adding the fitted response does not lower the error in capacity growth around its own mean (1.78 against 1.56 points). Every clean United quarter through 2026Q2 (34): +0.02 points (90% range -0.25 to +0.29) after 4 quarters. Delta, a second look on 16 clean quarters (5 before the pandemic, 11 in the test years): -0.98 points (90% range -1.87 to -0.08) after 4 quarters, below zero on 9 degrees of freedom: a hint of a cut, not a finding. United and Delta pooled (50 rows): -0.16 points (90% range -0.55 to +0.44).
unit: percentage points of year-over-year capacity (ASM) growth per 10% rise in the jet fuel price, cumulative through the stated number of quarters after the rise

primary_spec.description: Year-over-year capacity growth (percent) on year-over-year changes in the quarterly average spot jet fuel price (steps of 10%) at lags 0 to 4, with a linear time trend; fit years; pandemic-touched quarters excluded.
primary_spec.equation: growth[t] = a + sum_{j=0..4} b[j] * fuel change[t-j] + c * t + e[t]; cumulative response at k = b[0] + ... + b[k]
primary_spec.units: percentage points of year-over-year capacity (ASM) growth per 10% rise in the jet fuel price, cumulative through the stated number of quarters after the rise

selection.rule: lower BIC on the fit years

primary_spec.standard_errors: classical, scaled up by the largest ratio of Newey-West to classical variance among the cumulative responses when that ratio exceeds one; Student t intervals

curve_definition: p10/p50/p90 are quantiles of curve_draws; estimate, se, lo and hi are the regression's cumulative response, its standard error and its 90% Student t interval; lag_coef is the single quarter's coefficient.

curve_draws_method.method: Joint draws of the five lag coefficients from a multivariate Student t centred on the estimates; each row is the running sum of one draw, in the unit above. Not clipped: a draw may be positive or non-monotone.

united_points_definition: capacity_growth_pct is year-over-year growth in available seat miles; fuel_change_pct is the year-over-year change in the quarterly average Gulf Coast spot price.

delta_curve.description: Delta, same regressors, clean quarters before the pandemic and after it with a separate level after it and no trend (too few early quarters for one).
delta_curve.caveat: Delta's file starts in 2017Q4, so only 5 clean quarters precede the pandemic; the rest are test-year quarters. A second look, not a test.

pooled.interval: 90% percentile interval, moving-block bootstrap over quarters (blocks of 4, 1000 resamples)
pooled.description: United and Delta stacked on their clean quarters: common fuel lags, a level for each airline before and after the pandemic, and United's trend before it as in the primary specification.

without_trend.interval: 90% percentile interval, moving-block bootstrap over quarters (blocks of 4, 1000 resamples)

pooled.caveat: Both airlines face the same fuel series in the same quarters, so Delta's rows add little independent evidence, and the sample mixes fit and test years. Descriptive.

refit_through_latest.description: Every clean United quarter through the latest report: the primary specification with a separate level after the pandemic. Uses test-year quarters; descriptive, not the curve the simulator draws from.

select.note: No clean quarter: every quarter of 2020-2023 has its own level, its year-ago base or the base of a fuel lag inside 2020Q1-2021Q4.

by_split.definition: mae_no_response_pp and mae_with_response_pp compare capacity growth around the split's own mean with and without the primary fuel term (also taken around its own mean); no level or trend is carried across splits.

variants.description: Year-over-year capacity growth on year-over-year spot fuel changes at lags 0 to 4, with no other regressor; fit years.
Year-over-year capacity growth on year-over-year spot fuel changes at lags 0 to 4, with a linear time trend; fit years.
As the primary specification with United's reported average price per gallon in place of spot fuel; the reported price starts in 2013, so fewer quarters.

Looser pandemic rule on 2014-2023: an indicator for each quarter whose capacity or year-ago base falls in 2020Q1-2021Q4, which keeps the four quarters of 2023 (their fuel lags still reach into the pandemic and their growth is still the rebuild) with a level of their own. Not used: 2023 is not a clean year.

limits: Co-movement, not cause: fuel prices and travel demand move with the economy, and in the fitted years United's capacity growth trended up while fuel first fell and then rose. Nothing here identifies what fuel alone does to capacity.
24 quarters covering one fall and one rise in fuel; the fitted years contain no fuel shock of the size of 2022 or 2026.
The plain regression and the one with a time trend disagree in size; the trend is the difference. The primary is chosen by BIC on the fit years because the select years hold no clean quarter.
Schedules are set months ahead and fleet deliveries years ahead; a response slower than four quarters is outside the curve.
Fuel is the Gulf Coast spot average for the quarter, not United's own cost; hedges in 2013-2016 are not modelled.
A draw of the curve may be positive: the simulator should treat this as a response not told apart from zero, not as evidence that dearer fuel raises capacity.
Capacity is system available seat miles as reported; mainline and regional are not separated.
variants_tried: united_yoy_asm_on_spot_fuel_lags0_4_plain_fit: Year-over-year capacity growth on year-over-year spot fuel changes at lags 0 to 4, with no other regressor; fit years. n = 24; after 4 quarters +0.43 points (90% range +0.19 to +0.66).

united_yoy_asm_on_spot_fuel_lags0_4_trend_fit: Year-over-year capacity growth on year-over-year spot fuel changes at lags 0 to 4, with a linear time trend; fit years. n = 24; after 4 quarters +0.12 points (90% range -0.11 to +0.35).

reported_price: As the primary specification with United's reported average price per gallon in place of spot fuel; the reported price starts in 2013, so fewer quarters. n = 20; after 4 quarters +0.46 points (90% range +0.11 to +0.82).

pandemic_indicators_through_2023: Looser pandemic rule on 2014-2023: an indicator for each quarter whose capacity or year-ago base falls in 2020Q1-2021Q4, which keeps the four quarters of 2023 (their fuel lags still reach into the pandemic and their growth is still the rebuild) with a level of their own. Not used: 2023 is not a clean year. n = 28; after 4 quarters +0.14 points (90% range -0.22 to +0.51).

refit_through_latest: Every clean United quarter through the latest report: the primary specification with a separate level after the pandemic. Uses test-year quarters; descriptive, not the curve the simulator draws from. n = 34; after 4 quarters +0.02 points (90% range -0.25 to +0.29).

delta: Delta, same regressors, clean quarters before the pandemic and after it with a separate level after it and no trend (too few early quarters for one). n = 16; after 4 quarters -0.98 points (90% range -1.87 to -0.08).

pooled: United and Delta stacked on their clean quarters: common fuel lags, a level for each airline before and after the pandemic, and United's trend before it as in the primary specification. 50 rows; after 4 quarters -0.16 points (90% range -0.55 to +0.44).
pooled_without_trend: as pooled, without United's trend; after 4 quarters +0.14 points (90% range -0.17 to +0.64).
